newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt must not meddle with banks - Bank of E.Asia.
newsitem.headline: HK govt must not meddle with banks - Bank of E.Asia.

text.p: Bank of East Asia Ltd deputy chairman and chief executive David Li on Monday called on the Hong Kong government not to impose further restrictions on banks over residential mortgage lending.

He made the comment in response to the recommendation by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the territory's de facto central bank, that the maximum loan to value ratio for more expensive properties valued over HK$12 million should be cut to 60 percent from the current mortgage ceiling of 70 percent.
"I had a long conversation with Mr David Carse (HKMA's deputy chief executive)," Li told a news conference.
"I hope that he will not impose further restriction on banks because banks should have their own freedom to do what they know is best," Li said.
"I understand why the HKMA has to give some guidelines but I hope that the government will not interfere in commercial decision," he added.
Mortgage lending accounted for 45 percent of the bank's total loans last year.
The territory's property market has been soaring lately. Fears that speculation was driving prices higher have led to calls for government action.
But Li said the most effective way to control prices was for the government to increase land supply.
"I basically believe that because of supply and demand, our property prices are high...and I think the most effective way is to increase land supply," Li said.
Li said he did not expect the local property market to decline substantially.
"I can't see property prices going down a great deal," he said.
